title: Proof-of-need gated reservations and SLA assignment for Dedicated capacity
creator: Aisha Raman
body:
Problem: We regularly get reservation requests that are overspecified or not aligned with actual traffic, leading to wasted reserved throughput and manual rework during provisioning. Current intake and approval flow lacks a lightweight proof-of-need verification step and a deterministic mapping from requested throughput to SLA tier. This increases provisioning cycle time and causes capacity wastage for both the fleet and customers.

Goal: Introduce a proof-of-need gated reservation workflow that: (1) verifies basic usage expectations automatically before approval, (2) assigns a conditional SLA tier based on demonstrated need and contractual commitment, and (3) integrates with autoscaling policy templates and fleet allocation to reduce manual coordination.

Proposal (high level):
1) Intake form additions: add structured fields to the reservation request (requested_rps, 95th_percentile_token_rate_estimate, average_seq_len, expected_steady_state_duration_days, business_justification_url, billing_owner_email, compliance_tags). Add optional upload for a short runbook or customer-facing SLA expectations.
2) Automated proof-of-need check: a background job runs a lightweight verification for requests with an account history (recent hosted usage) — checks recent per-route throughput, token distributions, embedding vs. generate split. If an account has no history, trigger a trial requirement (probation window) instead of auto-approve.
3) Conditional SLA assignment: map verified requests to SLA bands (Bronze / Silver / Gold) based on verified 95p throughput and commitment length. SLA bands define latency SLOs, allowed burst factor, and decommit penalties.
4) Approval lanes: route requests to different approvers based on SLA band and size. Small, verified requests go through a 1-click Product Ops lane; large or unverified ones require Solutions Engineering and Finance signoff.
5) Autoscale policy binding: when a reservation is approved, apply a default autoscale template matched to the SLA band (e.g., Gold => aggressive scale targets with smaller buffer; Bronze => conservative autoscale + larger buffer). Templates are editable per-customer after onboarding.
6) Fleet allocation and buffer policy: capacity planner consumes the SLA-assigned throughput and reserves a deterministic buffer (configurable by fleet), enabling us to show a committed versus available capacity ledger in the console.
7) Probation and conversion: for accounts without usage history, provision a time-limited probation reservation (e.g., 2–4 weeks) sized at 50–75% requested throughput. If telemetry during probation matches the declared shape, auto-convert to full commit and upgrade SLA. If not, surface conversion playbook to account team.

Acceptance criteria (see separate field): the intake form, automated verifier, console UI changes, approval routing, autoscale template binding, and docs are implemented and validated in staging.

Open questions / trade-offs: automated verification accuracy for new workloads (LLM traffic shapes vary), how to calculate buffer (fixed percentage vs. probabilistic buffer), legal/finance impact of conditional SLAs and trial windows, and UX clarity for customers during probation.

Implementation notes: API change will add new params to the reservation create endpoint (see attachments for proposed schema). Console will need a new Reservation details page section showing "Verification status" and "SLA band (conditional / final)". Ops runbooks will include decommit and escalation flows.

Why this is different from existing intake work: rather than only focusing on approvals and manual checks, this introduces an automated verification layer plus explicit conditional SLA assignment tied to autoscale and fleet buffer behavior. The intent is to reduce provisioning time while preserving capacity predictability.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form additions are live in the console and API; new fields are validated and documented
Automated proof-of-need verifier runs on submission and returns a deterministic verdict (verified | probation_required | manual_review)
Reservation approval routing honors verifier output and SLA band mapping
Approved reservations automatically bind an autoscale policy template based on assigned SLA band
Probation flow provisions a time-limited reservation and a telemetry dashboard to evaluate conversion
Capacity planner view shows committed vs available capacity with buffer calculations
Playbooks for manual review, escalation, conversion, and decommit are written and linked
End-to-end staging test: create reservation for both "new" and "existing" accounts and exercise conversion path
comments: 2025-11-05 — Marco Li: Drafted proposal after sync with Solutions Eng. Added fields for telemetry and business justification. Leaving for PM review.
2025-11-12 — Aisha Raman: Feedback from Finance: need explicit billing_owner_email and automated cost estimate in intake. Added to form spec.

2025-11-20 — Priya Nair (Solutions Eng): Concerned about false negatives for novel workloads; suggested a probation with adaptive sizing instead of flat 50% sizing. Updated proposal to allow 50–75% range.

2025-11-28 — ENG-44210 owner (J. Ortega): Proposed verifier MVP uses recent hosted API logs and a simple heuristics engine (95p tokens, burst factor). We should instrument a feature flag for verifier rollout.
2025-12-02 — Design review (N. Park): Console mockups uploaded, requested clearer UI copy for 'Conditional SLA' vs 'Committed SLA'. Link in attachments.
2025-12-08 — Legal review request sent. Legal asked to review conversion language and decommit penalties for probation conversions. See attachments for legal notes.
2025-12-12 — Marco Li: Updated ACs and ready for engineering review. Assigned ENG-44210 as dependency. Please review autoscale template mappings in attachments.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy intake + API changes behind feature-flag + verifier in dry-run mode; validate telemetry for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (pilot): enable auto-verifier for 5 existing customers and run probation conversions manually; collect metrics on false positive/negative rates
Phase 3 (soft launch): enable auto-approve for verified small reservations and allow manual override for large/complex requests
Phase 4 (GA): open to self-serve with documentation, SLA contracts updated, and finance/legal hooks enabled
